title: fix(plugin-auth): a failed read in the last-administrator guard's default-slug capture rule answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, while auth-manager's sibling slug guard answers 503 for the same fault — give the read fault one code
body:
Filing gate **③**: a finding of the contract review of PR #25286 (#25271; record 6352123147, ① 4), carried on the #15212 ledger (6352526831). It is outside that PR's surface.
- **Who acts:** the shared queue.
- **Dedupe:** none.

## What is on `main`
- The last-administrator guard's `sys_organization` `beforeUpdate` rule (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts`, `guardOrganizationDefaultSlug`, from #25286) answers a read it cannot complete with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. That is the guard file's `failClosed` shape, and the text says the read failed and to retry.
- The sibling slug guard in `auth-manager.ts` answers the same kind of fault with 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`slugGuardReadFaultApiError`).
- So a caller cannot tell "you may not" from "try again" by code on this door.

## Wanted
- One code for a read fault across both guards. Most likely 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, or a dedicated code with its own row in `packages/spec`'s error-code ledger (ADR-0112).
- The refusal on the merits stays 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- Measure first: every half of the last-administrator guard uses `failClosed`. Say whether to change one half or the shared shape, because changing one half alone splits the guard's vocabulary.

## Acceptance
- A read fault answers the same code from both guards, pinned at the HTTP door (`organization/update`) and the engine door.
- A refusal on the merits is unchanged.
- R1–R4 hold.
